gaps.sentence: He ___ have driven so fast on that icy road — he is lucky to be unhurt.
gaps.explanation: 'Shouldn't have' criticizes dangerous past behavior: shouldn't have.

gaps.sentence: I really ___ stop drinking so much coffee; the doctor was very clear.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' can express strong obligation the speaker feels: must stop.

gaps.sentence: I ___ rather stay at home tonight, if that is all right.
gaps.explanation: 'Would rather' expresses preference: would rather stay.

gaps.sentence: Candidates ___ switch off their phones before the exam begins.
He ___ be at work — I've just seen him at the beach.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't' expresses something the evidence rules out.

gaps.sentence: You ___ better book now — the prices rise every week.
gaps.explanation: 'Had better' gives strong advice, often with urgency: had better book.

gaps.sentence: The lights are on, so they ___ be home.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' expresses a confident conclusion from evidence.

gaps.sentence: You ___ bring your own laptop — we will provide everything.
gaps.hint: no obligation, so needn't not mustn't
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' means it is not necessary; 'mustn't' would mean it is prohibited: needn't bring.
